title: KOSPI Close November 18, 2026: Rises 1.99% to 5,067.44, KOSDAQ +1.96%
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,067.44, up 1.99%, and KOSDAQ closed at 662.81, up 1.96%, after opening more than 2% higher on Nvidia's results and giving back most of the early gains. Aribio's Alzheimer's drug news, a Java security flaw, a Boston Dynamics tie-up and optical communications hopes drove individual stocks.

1. Rebound attempt on Nvidia results, gains largely reversed

KOSPI had closed Nov 17 at 4,968.48 (-2.59%), below 5,000. It opened at 5,098.82 (+2.62%), reached 5,133.14 (+3.31%), then fell as low as 4,943.17 (-0.51%) before closing at 5,067.44. KOSDAQ, which closed Nov 17 at 650.06 (-2.34%), opened at 664.93 (+2.29%), hit 674.30 (+3.73%) and dipped to 646.31 (-0.58%) before closing at 662.81.

Korean market coverage said Nvidia's third-quarter sales of $115.8 billion beat forecasts and that its fourth-quarter outlook was above expectations, reviving AI chip demand hopes. Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and SK Square rebounded, but heavy foreign selling in prior sessions and weak sentiment limited the gains, and KOSDAQ lost steam as individuals kept selling.

On KOSPI, institutions net bought about 507 billion won (provisional), while foreigners net sold about 334 billion won and individuals about 633 billion won. On KOSDAQ, institutions net bought about 177 billion won, while individuals net sold about 123 billion won and foreigners about 46 billion won.

2. Chips — large caps and KOSDAQ suppliers

Samsung Electro-Mechanics was also reported to have an Nvidia-related substrate supply deal, which was not independently confirmed.

3. Aribio AR1001 — Alzheimer's drug hopes

Aribio-related stocks surged after topline results from the global phase 3 trial of AR1001, an oral Alzheimer's drug candidate, were reported. Coverage said the drug slowed the worsening of dementia symptoms by 31% versus placebo in the monotherapy group. Samjin Pharmaceutical holds domestic manufacturing and exclusive sales rights. These figures come from reports and were not independently confirmed.

A high-severity flaw in Java, widely used in government and corporate systems, was reported with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2, and Oracle released a patch, raising hopes for security checks and replacement demand.

5. Robots — Boston Dynamics and GlobalFoundries

Hyundai Motor Group's Boston Dynamics was reported to be working with GlobalFoundries to test its Atlas humanoid robot in chip plants from early 2027, and to expand use of its Spot robot at overseas facilities. Robot-related stocks rose broadly; the larger movers are listed below.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Nov 18?
KOSPI closed at 5,067.44 (+1.99%) and KOSDAQ at 662.81 (+1.96%). Both rose more than 3% early and gave back most of the gains.

Why did Korean stocks open higher?
Nvidia's reported third-quarter sales of $115.8 billion and a stronger fourth-quarter outlook revived AI chip demand hopes.

Which stocks hit the upper limit?
Aribio Lab (Alzheimer's drug news) and Bigwave Robotics (robots) closed near +30%.
